design_detail: Cross-sectional postpartum depression screening program (telephone EPDS at 4–6 wk) with SCID diagnostic home visits for screen-positive women; descriptive statistics and chi-square comparisons only
severity_measure: No adjustment; descriptive screening/diagnostic prevalence study
comparison_group: None for main estimates (screen-negative women compared on demographics only)
population: Postpartum women (≥18 y, English-speaking) delivering at Magee-Womens Hospital, Pittsburgh, screened at 4–6 weeks postpartum
sample_size_detail: 826 screen-positive women with home SCID evaluation (basis of onset-timing and diagnosis estimates); 17,601 approached, 10,000 screened, 1,396 EPDS ≥10, 147 telephone MDD interviews; self-harm rates reported in 10,000 screened / 1,396 screen-positive
rationale: Authors call it a 'sequential case series', but it is a population screening/prevalence study with crude descriptive analyses only, so code 5 applies first. Main estimates (onset timing, primary diagnoses) come from the 826 home-visited women; the 10,000 screened is the broader descriptive sample.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort (planned secondary analysis), pre/post collaborative care implementation epochs without concurrent control; multivariable models with propensity score covariate adjustment and race-by-epoch interaction
severity_measure: Propensity score: maternal age, insurance, parity, tobacco, substance use history, chronic medical problem, any mental health history (presence only); no depression severity measure
comparison_group: Pre-implementation epoch; White individuals as referent for racial disparity
population: Pregnant/postpartum people self-identifying as Black or White receiving prenatal care at Northwestern Medicine (Chicago) collaborative-care practices; deliveries 2015–2016 and 2017–2019
sample_size_detail: Pre-implementation 2,286 (262 Black, 2,024 White); post-implementation 2,424 (313 Black, 2,111 White); treatment-recommendation outcome only among positive screens (pre 17 Black/9 White; post 41 Black/89 White)
rationale: Pre/post comparison without a concurrent control group, so per protocol not quasi-experimental; adjusted via propensity score. Covariates include only presence of a mental health history, not severity. Primary outcome (antenatal screening) modeled in all 4,710.

design_detail: Statewide population-based review of pregnancy-associated deaths from self-harm (death certificates, MMRC review, record abstraction); death ratios per 100,000 live births and descriptive frequencies, contextual crude comparison with all live births
comparison_group: None (descriptive contextual comparison with all Colorado women with live births)
population: Pregnancy-associated deaths from suicide or overdose in Colorado, 2004–2012
sample_size_detail: 211 maternal deaths; 63 from self-harm; 59 with detailed records abstracted (31 overdose, 28 suicide); 50 with toxicology; contextual comparison 614,154 women with live births
rationale: Authors label it a case series, but it is a registry-based descriptive analysis with population mortality ratios and a crude comparison to all live births, which fits code 5 before code 9. Descriptive analyses are of the 59 decedents with records.

design_detail: Prospective cohort (obstetric-practice recruitment, CIDI interviews in pregnancy and postpartum); Cox regression with time-dependent, 2-month-lagged antidepressant exposure; multivariable adjustment
severity_measure: Number of prior depressive episodes, onset before age 14, prior hospitalization for depression, major depressive episode in 6 months before pregnancy
comparison_group: Women with depression history not using antidepressants (time-varying)
population: Pregnant women with a history of depressive disorder recruited before 17 weeks from 137 obstetric practices in Connecticut and western Massachusetts, 2005–2009
sample_size_detail: Analytic sample restricted to women with prior depressive disorder; 9,525 screened, 3,517 invited, 2,793 interviewed; 130 used antidepressants during study period; 123 developed an MDE; 617 completed all interviews
rationale: Non-randomized cohort with adjusted Cox models (adjusted HR 0.88). Authors pre-selected covariates as 'correlates of severe depressive illness' (prior episodes, hospitalization, early onset).

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, US Medicaid Analytic eXtract claims; restricted to women with depression; logistic regression with propensity-score and high-dimensional propensity-score stratification
severity_measure: Proxies for depression severity: number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses, plus other psychotropic use, in PS/hdPS; depression-restricted cohort
comparison_group: Pregnant women with depression unexposed to antidepressants
population: Pregnant women in US Medicaid (46 states + DC), 2000–2010, and their infants; main estimate restricted to women with a depression diagnosis
sample_size_detail: Main SSRI estimate (hdPS OR 1.10): 65,315 SSRI-exposed vs 657,515 unexposed women with depression after PS trimming; non-SSRI comparison 16,274 vs 657,515; depression-restricted cohort 739,114; source cohort 3,789,330 pregnancies (102,179 SSRI, 26,771 non-SSRI)
rationale: Fully adjusted estimate is depression-restricted with PS/hdPS stratification; PS explicitly includes 'proxies for depression severity (number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses)'. No sibling analysis reported.

design_detail: Secondary analysis of 2 prospective observational cohorts; blinded Finnegan Scale exam at 2–4 weeks; chi-square/Kruskal-Wallis group comparisons plus multivariable logistic regression adjusting for preterm birth, race, age
severity_measure: Adjusted only for preterm birth, maternal race, and age; SIGH-ADS depression scores compared across groups but not adjusted for
comparison_group: Untreated mood disorder group and healthy unexposed comparison group
population: Mother-infant pairs from two NIMH-funded pregnancy cohorts (Cleveland, OH and Pittsburgh, PA), enrollment 2000–2011
rationale: Headline comparisons are crude, but the authors also report a multivariable logistic model (preterm birth, race, age; results not shown); under Amendment 2 the adjusted estimate is the fully adjusted one. No severity measure in the adjustment set.

design_detail: Single-center 6-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of sertraline with 1-week placebo lead-in
population: Women with postpartum-onset major depression (onset within 3 months of delivery), New Haven/southern Connecticut, recruited 1994–2004
sample_size_detail: 36 randomized (17 sertraline, 19 placebo) = ITT; 38 entered placebo lead-in (2 removed as placebo responders); 33 evaluable; 27 met strict DSM-IV 4-week onset criterion
rationale: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; primary analysis compared response rates in the ITT sample (n = 36).

design_detail: Systematic review and Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized trials of pharmacologic treatments for GAD (PROSPERO CRD42018087106)
population: Adult outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder in RCTs published 1994–2017
sample_size_detail: 89 RCTs; 25,441 patients randomized to 22 active drugs or placebo; 1,992 records screened
rationale: Network meta-analysis restricted to randomised clinical trials; not a perinatal population.

design_detail: Systematic review of 8 cohort studies to generate hypotheses, then population-based case-control study (malformed controls) in EUROCAT registries testing them; logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, birth year, and registry
severity_measure: Adjusted only for maternal age, year of birth, and reporting registry; authors note no data on epilepsy type or seizure frequency
comparison_group: No antiepileptic drug exposure (also valproic acid and other AED monotherapy); malformed controls (non-chromosomal and chromosomal)
population: Pregnancy outcomes (live births, fetal deaths ≥20 wk, terminations) in 19 European population-based congenital anomaly registries (EUROCAT), 1995–2005; plus 8 published cohort studies
sample_size_detail: Case-control analytic population: 11,790 cases (5 malformation groups) + 69,883 non-chromosomal + 11,763 chromosomal controls; 131 carbamazepine-monotherapy-exposed registrations; headline spina bifida estimate 2,048 cases vs 69,883 controls; source 98,075 registrations / 3,881,592 births; review: 8 cohorts, 2,680 exposed pregnancies
rationale: Review served to identify 'indications' that were tested in the case-control study, which yields the main estimates (spina bifida OR 2.6), so the case-control analysis is primary. Adjustment omits epilepsy severity; authors state they lacked 'type of epilepsy, frequency of seizures'.

design_detail: Retrospective population-based drug-utilization study in 11 US health plans (MEPREP), pharmacy dispensing linked to birth certificates; prevalence and trends only
comparison_group: Deliveries without antipsychotic exposure (descriptive characteristics only)
population: Live-born deliveries to women aged 15–45 enrolled in 11 US health plans (incl. Tennessee Medicaid), 2001–2007
sample_size_detail: 4,223 atypical antipsychotic-exposed, 548 typical antipsychotic-exposed, 514,782 with no antipsychotic use (60 days before pregnancy through delivery)
rationale: Purely descriptive prevalence/trend analysis of prenatal antipsychotic use with no effect estimate or adjustment.

design_detail: Prospective longitudinal cohort; repeated-measures mixed models of Bayley (BSID-II) scores at 12, 26, 52 weeks; Model II/III adjusted for maternal symptom scores and selected confounders
severity_measure: SIGH-ADS depression and Mania Rating Scale scores (Models II and III), plus maternal age, education, marital status where indicated
comparison_group: Untreated bipolar disorder (BD−) and unexposed women without bipolar disorder
population: Pregnant women with bipolar disorder (treated or untreated) and unexposed controls and their infants, Pittsburgh, PA, 2006–2011
sample_size_detail: 54 BD+ (psychotropic-treated), 27 BD− (untreated), 116 nonexposed controls; assessment completion varied by group (e.g., 28 BD+, 20 BD−, 96 controls with MDI/PDI at 52 wk)
rationale: Non-randomized cohort; fully adjusted Model III includes SIGH-ADS and Mania Rating Scale symptom scores, which are severity measures for the bipolar indication. Abstract headline P values come from the unadjusted Model I.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (MOOSE/PRISMA) of metabolic syndrome prevalence, with relative-risk meta-analyses and meta-regression
comparison_group: Between diagnostic groups; matched general population controls; antipsychotic-naive participants
population: Adults with schizophrenia/related psychotic disorders, bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder (any setting)
sample_size_detail: 198 studies, 52,678 unique people with severe mental illness; population-based subset 29 studies (n = 18,594)
rationale: Meta-analysis of observational (cross-sectional, retrospective, prospective) prevalence studies; inclusion also allowed baseline data from RCTs, but the number of RCTs is not stated. Full text in file is the Spanish edition.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract; restricted to women with depression; logistic regression with propensity-score stratification (hdPS confirmatory)
severity_measure: Proxies for depression severity: number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses in PS; depression-restricted cohort
comparison_group: Women with depression unexposed to antidepressants in the first trimester
population: Pregnant women in US Medicaid (46 states + DC), 2000–2007, and their liveborn infants; main estimate restricted to women with depression
sample_size_detail: Fully adjusted SSRI estimate (RR 1.06): 36,778 SSRI-exposed vs 180,564 unexposed women with depression after PS trimming; source cohort 949,504 pregnancies (64,389 antidepressant-exposed incl. 46,144 SSRI; 885,115 unexposed); other classes analyzed separately
rationale: PS stratification within the depression-restricted cohort explicitly controls 'proxies for depression severity (number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses)'. Robust variance for repeat pregnancies is not a within-mother analysis.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, US Medicaid Analytic eXtract; restricted to women with depression; GEE relative risks with multivariable adjustment (hdPS sensitivity analysis)
severity_measure: Proxies of depression severity: number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses
comparison_group: Women with depression unexposed to antidepressants (secondary: SSRI monotherapy active comparator)
population: Pregnant women with depression in US Medicaid, 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: Primary analysis: 26,548 exposed (19,000 SSRI, 1,216 SNRI, 441 tricyclic, 2,622 bupropion, 647 other monotherapy; 2,622 polytherapy) + 59,219 unexposed; depression cohort 100,942 minus 15,175 first-trimester-only users; source 1,248,875 pregnancies
rationale: Fully adjusted models include depression-severity proxies (outpatient/inpatient depression diagnosis counts) within a depression-restricted cohort. Table 2 counts sum to 85,767 analyzed.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Kaiser Permanente Washington EHR linked to state birth records; continuers vs discontinuers among prior antidepressant users; GEE with inverse probability of treatment weighting
severity_measure: IPTW includes psychotherapy and psychiatry visits, inpatient psychiatric hospitalization, psychotropic fills, described as 'indicators of mental health severity'; PHQ-9 described only
comparison_group: Prior antidepressant users who discontinued in pregnancy
population: Singleton live births 2001–2014 to Kaiser Permanente Washington members with an antidepressant fill ≤6 months before pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 1,634 continuers vs 1,211 discontinuers in GDM analysis; ~4% with missing covariates excluded from complete-case regression (exact analytic N not reported); blood glucose subset 1,101
rationale: Active-comparator restriction plus IPTW on mental health utilization and hospitalization severity indicators. N is the eligible GDM cohort; the complete-case regression N is not given exactly.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, US Medicaid Analytic eXtract; restricted to women with mood/anxiety disorders; GEE relative risks with multivariable adjustment plus hdPS analysis
severity_measure: Proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity: number of outpatient and inpatient mood/anxiety diagnoses
comparison_group: Women with mood/anxiety disorders unexposed to antidepressants in the 5 months before delivery
population: Pregnant women aged 12–55 with mood or anxiety disorder diagnoses in US Medicaid, 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: 106,000 with mood/anxiety disorder minus 3,278 polytherapy; SRI current 12,710, recent 6,096, past 10,416; non-SRI current 1,495, recent 829, past 2,132; unexposed 69,044; hdPS trimmed 10,203 vs 53,348; source 2,759,414 pregnancies
rationale: Fully adjusted GEE models include 'proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity' (diagnosis counts) in a disorder-restricted cohort. Robust variance for repeat pregnancies is not a within-mother analysis.
